newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurance claims eased in 95 - association.
newsitem.headline: German insurance claims eased in 95 - association.

text.p: Claims levels eased in the German insurance industry in 1995 after years of "partly catastrophic" payouts, the GDV insurance association said on Monday.

In a leaflet outlining finalised 1995 data for GDV members, which include all leading German life and non-life insurance companies, the association said lower claims on car, household, property, storm and glass risks led to an overall improvement.
However payouts rose again for burglaries, fires, industrial third-party, insolvencies and legal disputes.
Overall underwriting earnings in car insurance were particularly satisfactory at 1.8 billion marks, GDV said. It did not give a comparative figure.
Final figures showed GDV members posted a 5.9 percent increase in premium income to 218.7 billion marks in 1995, boosted in particular by interest in private pensions.
The association said the weak German economy and rising unemployment had depressed business in the period.
